verdicts.summary: Lean has an equivalent formula. All three formulas are present, reached by instantiating general lemmas rather than written out. In normalized_global_solution the competitor at viscosity ν is pushed through rescale_global_solution with a = (√ν)⁻¹: the velocity field is rescale a a⁻¹ v_ν = fun z => ν^{-1/2} • v_ν (z.1, √ν • z.2), which is the paper's v(y,t) = ν^{-1/2} v_ν(√ν y, t) after inv_inv and (√ν)⁻¹ = ν^{-1/2} (ν > 0); the pressure field is rescale (a²) a⁻¹ P_ν = fun z => ν^{-1} • P_ν (z.1, √ν • z.2), the paper's P(y,t) = ν^{-1} P_ν(√ν y, t). The resulting viscosity is a²·ν = 1 (hcoef), matching the paper's 'viscosity-one competitor'. The energy identity follows from kineticEnergy_spatial_smul at a = ν^{-1/2}, b = √ν: ‖a‖² · |(b³)⁻¹| = ν^{-1} · ν^{-3/2} = ν^{-5/2}, the paper's factor; Lean's kineticEnergy has a 1/2 that cancels on both sides. Notational differences only: Lean orders spacetime as (t, x); the Lean pipeline uses the inequality form UniformFiniteEnergy.spatial_smul where the paper states the exact identity, the exact identity being available as kineticEnergy_spatial_smul; and the paper writes the competitor pressure as capital P_ν here against lowercase p_ν in (10.22).
